newsitem.title: USA: Trial date set for Florida tobacco lawsuit.
newsitem.headline: Trial date set for Florida tobacco lawsuit.

text.p: A Miami judge on Thursday set a Sept. 8, 1997, trial date in a landmark class-action lawsuit brought by a physician who claims he became sick from smoking.

Dade Circuit Judge Alan Postman issued an order setting the trial date and a notification procedure in the case, which was filed more than two years ago by Dr. Howard Engle, a Miami physician stricken by emphysema.

It is the latest in a series of high-profile lawsuits against the tobacco industry in Florida. A separate class-action lawsuit brought by a nationwide group of flight attendants against the industry is set for trial next June 2.
"The judge gave a combination of what we thought was reasonable and what the tobacco companies thought was reasonable," Stanley Rosenblatt, an attorney for the plaintiffs in the case, said.

Individual letters will be issued to 38,000 Florida physicians urging them to inform their patients of the lawsuit, the ruling said. Notices will also be published in 68 Florida newspapers beginning January 2, and in the regional edition of TV Guide magazine.
"This is a very fair notification procedure and should alert everyone who is not a hermit about this lawsuit," Rosenblatt said.
As many as 500,000 Florida smokers could be eligible to join the class-action lawsuit, he said.
The state of Florida also has a lawsuit pending against tobacco makers in an effort to recover almost $1 billion in Medicaid treatment costs. That case is set to go to trial next year on August 4.

Earlier this autumn, the tobacco industry was dealt a major blow when a jury in Jacksonville, Florida, awarded $750,000 to Grady Carter, a former smoker with lung cancer who claimed that cigarettes caused his illness. The case is being appealed.
Tobacco companies involved in the Florida cases include R.J. Reynolds, a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp, and B.A.T Industries.
